title: The Menstrual Cycle: Hormonal Cascades & LH Surge
quickSummary: Menstrual cycle: Menstrual (1-5), Follicular (6-13, estrogen repair), Ovulatory (Day 14, massive LH Surge releases 2° oocyte), and Luteal (15-28, Corpus Luteum secretes progesterone to maintain secretory endometrium).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Menstrual cycle: Menstrual phase (Days 1-5: low progesterone, sloughing of stratum functionale), Follicular phase (Days 6-13: FSH matures follicles, estrogen rebuilds endometrium), Ovulatory phase (Day 14: Estrogen positive feedback -> massive LH Surge -> ovulation of 2° oocyte arrested in Metaphase II), Luteal phase (Days 15-28: Corpus Luteum secretes high progesterone; if no fertilization -> Corpus Albicans, progesterone drops, menstruation repeats).

conceptBreakdown.content:
The Menstrual Cycle is the cyclic series of physiological modifications in the primate female reproductive system (averaging $\approx 28\text{ days}$), controlled by the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Ovarian axis.

### 5.1 Menstrual Phase Dynamics

1. **Menstrual Phase (Days 1–5)**: Degeneration of the Corpus Luteum from the previous cycle causes a sharp collapse in Progesterone and Estrogen. The functional mucosal layer of the endometrium (*Stratum Functionale*) breaks down, sloughing off with $50\text{--}80\text{ mL}$ of blood and tissue fluid.
2. **Follicular / Proliferative Phase (Days 6–13)**: Anterior pituitary **FSH** stimulates primary follicles to grow into mature Graafian follicles. Proliferating theca and granulosa cells synthesize rising levels of **Estrogens**, stimulating rapid mitotic renewal, vascularization, and thickening of the endometrium.
3. **Ovulatory Phase (Day 14)**: High sustained estrogen levels ($>200\text{ pg/mL}$ for $>36\text{ hours}$) switch feedback from negative to positive, triggering a massive, rapid peak in pituitary LH secretion (**LH Surge**).
   - **Consequences of LH Surge**:
     - Stimulates the primary oocyte to complete Meiosis I.
     - Causes proteolytic enzymes (collagenase) to weaken the ovarian tunica albuginea, rupturing the Graafian follicle to release the Secondary Oocyte (Ovulation).
4. **Luteal / Secretory Phase (Days 15–28)**: LH luteinizes the collapsed follicle into the **Corpus Luteum ("Yellow Body")**, which synthesizes large quantities of **Progesterone** (and estrogen). Progesterone transforms the endometrium into a glandular, glycogen-secreting vascular bed ready for blastocyst implantation.
   - **Absence of Fertilization**: Progesterone and estrogen exert negative feedback on LH/FSH. Deprived of LH support, the Corpus Luteum degenerates into white scar tissue (**Corpus Albicans**), steroid levels crash, and menses begins.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Estrogen Biphasic Feedback
conceptBreakdown.title: Estrogen Biphasic Feedback
conceptBreakdown.content: Low to moderate levels of estrogen exert negative feedback on FSH/LH secretion. High, sustained levels at the end of the follicular phase trigger positive feedback on GnRH and LH release, causing the ovulatory LH surge.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Body Temperature Shift
conceptBreakdown.title: Body Temperature Shift
conceptBreakdown.content: Progesterone acting on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center causes a distinct basal body temperature increase of ~0.3°C to 0.5°C immediately following ovulation, used in rhythm fertility tracking.
